summary: 100-ft Aermotor fire tower in Bluff Park, Hoover, Alabama; tower removed 1992, restored cab on display on Patton Chapel Road. Build date differs across sources.

facts.design: 100-foot steel Aermotor tower with an observation cab
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1992; the restored cab is displayed in a small park on Patton Chapel Road, Hoover

access.note: Hoover Sun describes a drive-up cab with a historic marker on site; no hours or permit rules found

events.note: May 1, 1941 item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page calls the tower new; named for George Gordon Crawford. The Hoover Sun's 63-year span points to about 1929 instead
National Geodetic Survey description (1971) still describes the state fire lookout tower, about 100 feet high
Tower torn down and misplaced; cab removed and hidden on city property

A member of the Hoover Fire Department found the cab on a lot at Fire Station No. 4; a restoration project that began May 2011 was completed by a partnership between the Historical Society and the City of Hoover
Cab placed in a small park at 1591 Patton Chapel Road, across from Hoover Fire Station No. 2
Restored cab dedicated October 31; Sun report dated December 31, 2012
Registered May 27, 2016 as US 1614, AL 3; nominated by Andrew Zerbe

corrections.why: The tower came down in 1992, but its cab survives and is shown on Patton Chapel Road; 'gone' suggests nothing remains

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A May 1, 1941 item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page calls the tower new. The Hoover Sun says it stood 63 years before its 1992 removal, which would put its start around 1929. The story reports both and does not choose.

sources.title: Partnership leads to preservation of Bluff Park icon

notes_for_editor: Hoover Historical Society page (hooverhistoricalsociety.org/historical-sites/crawford-bluff-park-fire-tower-cab/) returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text. Its search snippet gives a 1939 build date, a 1992 airplane-cost reason and a 1992 cab transfer from the Alabama Forestry Commission; none of that is cited because it was not read. Worth checking by hand. No staffing or fire-specific records for this tower were found. The access claim rests on the Sun's quote about walking up to the cab; no official hours or access policy was found.
